title: Codebook wording review: Record-keeping on every row
background:
Review round 4 of the codebook wording. You chose on 30 October that agents draft the missing value definitions and you review every wording slot here. This page covers **record-keeping on every row**.

Each card is one codebook item. Open "Show the wording slots" to read them. Each slot is labelled with where its text came from:

- **Plan text**
- **New agent draft (round 4)**
- **Option text you chose in round 3**
- **Agent edit of the signed questionnaire**
- **Text you approved on 30 October**
- **Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete**

Answer per item: approve all, approve with line-edits or deletions in the comments (by slot number), or ask for a redraft. Deletion is open only for old version-2.5 slots and for one slot of each overlap pair. The batch card at the top approves everything you leave unmarked. No recommendation is given on any wording.

New agent drafts carry a certainty mark; those marked **Needs your decision** rest on no ruling or text for some point.

items.title: support entailment
items.situation:
Question: 'Does this text state that <field> is <value>?'

Recorded on every row.

4 slots: 2 × plan text; 2 × new agent draft (round 4).
items.body:
**1. Question** — Plan text, from review round 1
'Does this text state that <field> is <value>?'

**2. Value `true`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The quoted text states that the field has the given value.
_Draft certainty: high._

**3. Value `false`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The quoted text does not state that the field has the given value. The answer's support status becomes 'downgraded: quote does not state the value'.
_Draft certainty: high._

**4. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
State = quote (plus a short window); question: 'Does this text state that <field> is <value>?' true/false; false or confidence < threshold -> downgrade `no_support`.

items.title: supporting text
items.situation:
Recorded on every row.

4 slots: 4 × plan text.
items.body:
**1. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
For every jev code on a page or activity, the extractor (C-001; the quote step) extracts the verbatim supporting text from the page. RC-D-002 row 15 replaces "after jev has coded": the quote step never sees the answer for the field it quotes, but may see that a gate is not `none` (r2#18). The quote step runs for every activity, including items the applicability table skips; those copies are kept internally, and the item is published as "not asked" (activity-07 b). A01 and CX-61 get quotes relevant to the field. The scale number (A09) is copied verbatim by the quote step and the classifier picks the unit (C4 a); the publication date (X26) is coded by the quote step under the R-042 check. X35 adds an entailment check per (code, quote) with a chosen-answer probability bar (r2#26).

**2. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
Supporting text is checked against the stored page text by fuzzy match; a quote below the match threshold counts as no supporting text.

**3. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
Supporting text is published with the code it supports. The API carries the full text; the website shows it up to a display cap, with a marker and access to the full text.

**4. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
Published supporting quotes stay verbatim, with no masking.

**1. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
A manifest (contract versions, `JEV_QUESTION_SET_VERSION`, jev model, extractor model id + prompt SHA-256, chunker + estimator version, matcher + threshold, confidence threshold, codebook item hashes) keyed by `instrument_id` on every row.

**2. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
Every jev answer is stored with its probability distribution, confidence, response model id and request id. RC-D-002 row 12: every automated coder (classifier, quote step, detector, mechanical rules) stores coder type, model, version and request id (P10a); the per-run version record holds the codebook version, and per-code coder details are internal and linked to it (r2#57); the row carries the codebook version + setup pointer (r2#32); the classifier record keeps the chosen-answer probability (r2#26).

items.title: support status second reason
items.situation:
Recorded on every row.

5 slots: 3 × new agent draft (round 4); 1 × option text you chose in round 3; 1 × text you approved on 30 October.
items.body:
**1. Value `downgraded_no_quote`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The answer also failed because it has no supporting quote.
_Draft certainty: medium._ **Needs your decision:** Under the approved order (quote check first, then the 0.8 bar), a missing quote is always the main reason, so this value seems never to occur as the second reason. Please confirm the value list or the order.

**2. Value `downgraded_low_confidence`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The answer also failed because the classifier's certainty was below the 0.8 bar.
_Draft certainty: high._

**3. Value `downgraded_quote_not_stating_value`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The answer also failed because its quote does not state the value.
_Draft certainty: medium._ **Needs your decision:** Same as 'no quote': the quote-meaning check is part of the quote check, which comes first, so this seems never to be the second reason. Please confirm.

**4. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
A second reason item

**5. Rule** — Text you approved on 30 October
Values: downgraded_no_quote, downgraded_low_confidence, downgraded_quote_not_stating_value. The main status takes the first failed check in check order (quote, then the 0.8 bar); the second item takes the other; empty when only one reason holds.
